title: Cell-class marker heatmap
caption: Wilcoxon one-vs-rest differential expression across the 10 annotated classes (n=913 cells) recovers canonical markers — e.g. Slc17a7 for excitatory neurons, Slc32a1 for interneurons, Laptm5 for microglia; heatmap shows per-class mean log-normalized expression, z-scored across classes, for the top 5 markers per class.
question: Which genes define each cell type in this tissue?

title: Volcano: excitatory vs inhibitory neurons
caption: Wilcoxon test, Excitatory neuron (n=337) vs Interneuron (n=60): 102 genes up and 43 down at BH-adjusted p<0.05 and |log2FC|>1.0; top excitatory genes Slc17a7, Lingo1, Tbr1, top interneuron genes Slc32a1, Pcp4l1, Slc6a1.
question: What separates excitatory from inhibitory neurons here?

title: Spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I)
caption: Moran's I on a k=6 nearest-neighbor spatial graph over all 10,000 genes (n=913 cells): Shank1 ranks first at I=0.83 (permutation z=46, p=0.001, 999 perms), followed by Slc17a7 (I=0.80) and Eef1a2 (I=0.79); expected I under no structure is -0.0011.
question: Which genes show the strongest spatial patterning?

title: Spatial map of Shank1
caption: Cells plotted at their recorded x,y centroids colored by log-normalized Shank1 expression — the most spatially autocorrelated gene in the dataset (Moran's I=0.83 vs expected -0.0011; permutation p=0.001).
question: Where is Shank1 expressed in the tissue?

title: Neighborhood enrichment matrix
caption: Observed vs expected spatial adjacency between cell classes (z-scores from 1000 label permutations on a symmetric k=6 kNN graph, seed 0): Choroid Plexus cells self-aggregate most strongly (z=45); the top cross-class association is Neuroblast-Neural Stem (z=14), while Excitatory neuron-Neuroblast are most spatially segregated (z=-20).
